study: Ofner, Schwarz, Pereira and Müller-Putz (2017), DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0182578. Source recordings DOI 10.5281/zenodo.834976, CC BY 4.0.
question: For each instruction, quarter-second window and instrument channel, how many of seven people have a reading above, below or equal to their own pre-cue reading?
source_checks: Use only the 21 enumerated original execution files. Verify whole-file hashes and expected header, native channel order, 512 Hz/64 Hz sample grids and aligned 512 Hz event clock. For each run require six distinct cue onsets per code, each with one end 1536 ticks later. An unexpected file, layout or census stops the cohort build for investigation; no substitution or reduction of the cohort.
run_channel_quality: For each channel in each run, inspect all finite stored samples of that channel. Fewer than two distinct finite values makes that run/channel unusable for every cue and window. An entirely constant channel is unavailable even if its trial contrasts are zero. A constant trial or window on a varying channel remains eligible. No dispersion cutoff or tolerance.
trial: The cue tick is the one-based GDF event position minus one. Every time interval is half-open; convert both endpoint ticks to the channel's native grid by integer ceiling(tick * channel_rate / 512). For a valid run/channel, subtract the median of the baseline samples from the median of the window samples within each trial. Require both full intervals in bounds, nonempty and entirely finite. No interpolation, rereferencing, artifact correction, normalization or feature selection.
person: For each run take the median trial contrast among eligible repeats of the specified cue, requiring at least three of six. Require three qualifying run medians and take their equally weighted arithmetic mean. Exclude that person for that cell if any run/channel fails quality or repeat coverage. A strictly positive mean counts as higher, strictly negative as lower, exactly zero (including signed zero) as unchanged. No rounding, thresholding or sign inference from a cue name.
group: Report integer counts higher, lower, unchanged, unavailable. Valid = higher + lower + unchanged. The four counts sum to seven. Group marker colour uses (higher - lower)/valid. Positive is orange, negative blue, equal counts neutral; zero valid is grey. The scale compares signs among available people. Show valid/seven and the complete counts wherever the counts are read. A saturated colour can arise from few valid people. Report every prespecified cell (7 cues x 4 windows x 67 channels); retain all contrary, null and unavailable cells.
scope: Descriptive comparison in seven fitting participants. All had three execution runs in scope. Only the previously published S1 view was known when the group calculation was frozen. Counts have units of people; within-person comparisons use original stored units with no verified physical units or anatomical sign. Electrical observations include reference, eye, muscle and movement effects. The drawing illustrates the instruction. This analysis does not estimate cortical sources, anatomical movement direction, force, causal effects, prediction or population generalization.
disclosure: Release only integer cohort counts and public method, channel metadata, source identities and licences. Do not include per-person values or classifications, run values, trial features, timings or signal traces in the new group product.
verification: Rebuild all cells from original files, separately implement the parser/reduction to compare all counts, exercise true zero, missing, constant, insufficient-repeat and timing boundaries, and compare the extracted offline reader and its launch inventory against the built public product.
